title: Lemma: number of parts equal to k equals sum_m p(n-km) (proves (ii))

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (heart of the TRUE direction, identity (ii)).**

Prove the classical "number of parts equal to $k$" identity:
$$N_k(n):=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\operatorname{mult}_k(\lambda)=\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-km),$$
where $\operatorname{mult}_k(\lambda)$ is the number of parts of $\lambda$ equal to $k$, $p$ is the partition function (with $p(0)=1$, $p(<0)=0$), and the sum over $m$ is finite ($km\le n$).

Equivalently, as a generating function,
$$\sum_{n\ge1}N_k(n)x^n=\Big(\prod_{j\ge1}\tfrac1{1-x^j}\Big)\frac{x^k}{1-x^k}.$$

**Why this closes (ii):** Writing $Q_k:=q^{k^\alpha}$, the LHS of (ii) has
$[x^n]=\sum_{k\ge1}N_k(n)Q_k$, while the common RHS has $[x^n]=\sum_{k\ge1}Q_k\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-km)$ (using $\tfrac{x^k}{1-x^k}=\sum_{m\ge1}x^{km}$ and $P(x)=\sum_j p(j)x^j$). So (ii) is equivalent to $N_k(n)=\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-km)$ for all $k,n$.

**Suggested proof:** $N_k(n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\sum_{m\ge1}\mathbf 1[\operatorname{mult}_k(\lambda)\ge m]=\sum_{m\ge1}\#\{\lambda\vdash n:\operatorname{mult}_k(\lambda)\ge m\}$, and the map "delete $m$ copies of the part $k$" is a bijection onto all partitions of $n-km$, giving $p(n-km)$.

Verified numerically: $N_k(n)=\sum_m p(n-km)$ for all $n\le 12$.
